task_description:
description: Develop a multi-agent simulation system that models the spread of mask-wearing behavior through social networks.
simulation_focus: Predict agents' mask-wearing behavior over day 30 - day 39 (last ten days) based on their attributes, social connections, and past behavior
Model information propagation and behavioral changes triggered by social influence and government intervention starting on Day 10

overview.phenomenon_and_objectives: We study the diffusion and maintenance of mask-wearing behavior through interpersonal social networks in a city-scale population (N ~ 10^4–10^5 agents) over 40 daily time steps (Day 0–Day 39), with government intervention commencing on Day 10. Key participants are individual citizens embedded in multi-layer networks (household, workplace/school, community ties) and a policy authority broadcasting information and enforcing mandates. The primary objective is predictive: forecast each agent’s binary mask-wearing state and the aggregate adoption rate during Days 30–39 given observed attributes, past behaviors (Days 0–29), network structure, and policy history. Secondary objectives are descriptive (reproduce typical adoption curves and cascade patterns) and policy evaluation (compare intervention timing/intensity and targeting to maximize adoption and minimize disparities). Success is measured by: (a) agent-level predictive accuracy—AUC/PR-AUC, Brier score, log-loss, and calibration error (ECE); (b) aggregate trajectory fit—RMSE/MAE and DTW similarity between simulated and observed daily adoption rates; (c) coverage and width of 80–95% predictive intervals; (d) time to reach adoption thresholds (50%/70%/90%); and (e) subgroup fairness gaps across age/income/degree quantiles. Decision levers include policy start day (baseline Day 10), mandate strength/intensity in [0,1], enforcement probability/coverage (%), fine level ($), information campaign intensity and targeting (global vs. high-degree nodes), and mask supply/subsidy levels; optional network-level levers include seeding influencers and limiting large gatherings. Exogenous inputs include epidemic risk indicators (case rates), weather/seasonality, exogenous media sentiment, baseline demographics, the fixed social network topology, day-of-week effects, and exogenous shocks (mask shortages). The model outputs per-step aggregates (overall and subgroup adoption rates, switching rates, cascade sizes) and agent-level states with uncertainty quantification to support cross-scenario comparison and policy scoring.
overview.scale_and_granularity: scale_and_granularity: The simulator updates every 1 day for 40 steps (Day 0–Day 39). Spatial representation is aspatial, centered on a multi-layer social network (household, workplace/school, community); an optional secondary POI labeling (home, workplace, school) annotates nodes/edges for reporting and targeting but does not model physical movement. The population is a synthetic city-scale sample with N ≈ 10^4–10^5 agents (default 75,000), matched to observed age/income/household-size/degree distributions; it can be downsampled with expansion weights for speed or scaled up linearly. This resolution aligns with daily behavior/policy data, captures day-of-week effects, and preserves cascade dynamics while keeping computation tractable.
overview.agent_archetypes:
agent_archetypes: Two archetypes operate on a daily tick (Day 0–Day 39) over a fixed, multilayer social network (household, workplace/school, community). Primary: Residents (citizens, including students and retirees). Secondary: Policy Authority (government).

Residents
- Roles
  - Household member (intra-household influence and coordination).
  - Worker/Student (workplace/school layer ties active mainly Mon–Fri).
  - Community member (friendship/neighbor ties).
  - Optional Influencer role (subset with higher reach/credibility and larger daily messaging budget).
- Internal state (per agent, time-varying unless noted)
  - mask_state_t ∈ {0,1}; last-switch-day; intention score (latent utility).
  - Habit/inertia strength h_i; memory of enforcement (fine_received_within_τ); fatigue/discomfort cost c_i,t.
  - Perceived layer-specific masking prevalence p̂_i,l(t) with exponential decay memory (e.g., half-life 7 days).
  - Perceived epidemic risk r̂_i(t) from city case rates and media sentiment; trust weights by channel (household/work/community/government).
  - Mask inventory m_i,t (units), procurement lead-time L_i (days), affordability threshold relative to income y_i; subsidy eligibility flag.
  - Socio-demographics: age, income quintile, household size and role (guardian/child), education, health vulnerability, degree per layer, centrality; psychosocial traits: conformity ω_i, pro-sociality φ_i, risk sensitivity κ_i, government trust τ_i, media trust μ_i.
- Observation (capability boundary)
  - Sees own past actions and m_i,t exactly.
  - Observes neighbor mask states on active edges with noise and a 1-day lag: for each edge (i,j,l), visibility v_l ∈ [0.6,1.0] and misclassification ε_l ∈ [0,0.1]; computes p̂_i,l(t) from last k days (default k=7) with decay.
  - Receives broadcast policy signals (mandate intensity in [0,1], enforcement coverage/probability, fine level, subsidy/supply announcements) and city-level indicators (case rate, day-of-week, weather/seasonality, media sentiment). Observation may be filtered by τ_i, μ_i (trust) and stochastic exposure of campaign messages.
  - Does not observe future interventions; no access to global network structure.
- Communication
  - Implicit signaling via observable mask_state on active edges.
  - Optional explicit interpersonal messaging along edges with daily budget B_i (default 5; influencers 20), per-edge send probability σ_l (household > workplace > community) and reception trust weights; messages carry normative cues and perceived risk, attenuated by trust and noise.
  - No platform-wide broadcasting by residents.
- Mobility
  - Aspatial; no movement. Edge activation varies by day: workplace/school edges active Mon–Fri (α_work=0.9 weekday, 0.1 weekend), community edges slightly higher on weekends (α_comm=1.2 weekend, 0.8 weekday); household edges always active (α_home=1.0).
- Transactions
  - Procure masks when m_i,t < desired buffer b_i (e.g., 5 units): attempt purchase with probability dependent on supply S_t and affordability (price P_t after subsidy vs budget). If purchase fails, backorder with delay L_i. Inventory depletes by 1 per day if masked; if m_i,t=0, masking constrained unless cloth/DIY option available at higher discomfort cost c_i,t.
- Collaboration
  - Household coordination: minors (e.g., age < 13) mirror guardian majority with probability ρ_home; partners exhibit correlated choices via higher ω_i on household edges.
- Competition
  - None strategic; social pressure/sanctions modeled via normative utility and perceived disapproval; enforcement is probabilistic, not adversarial.
- Resources & constraints
  - Time: daily decision; messaging budget B_i; procurement attempts ≤1/day.
  - Money/budget: affordability affects procurement; fines reduce future affordability and temporarily boost perceived enforcement.
  - Regulations: mandates from Day 10 onward with varying intensity; noncompliance may incur fines with probability set by enforcement coverage.
- Decision policy (primary)
  - Probabilistic threshold/utility rule with inertia and social influence:
    - U_i(t) = β0_i + β_H h_i·1[mask_{t-1}=1] + β_S Σ_l w_l·p̂_i,l(t-1)·ω_i + β_R κ_i·r̂_i(t-1) + β_G τ_i·Mandate_t·E[Enforce_t]·Fine_t − β_C c_i,t − β_P NetPrice_t(y_i, subsidy_t) + β_M μ_i·MediaSent_t + ε_i,t
    - P(mask_i,t=1) = sigmoid(U_i(t)), subject to feasibility m_i,t>0 or DIY option. If caught noncompliant, update fine_received_within_τ and temporarily increase E[Enforce].
  - Secondary mechanisms
    - Habit formation: h_i increases with consecutive masked days; fatigue raises c_i,t after long streaks, decaying with rest days.
    - Targeted responsiveness: influencers have larger β_S and outward communication; high-degree agents receive more campaign exposures.
- Action set (daily; discrete)
  - Choose mask_state_t ∈ {0,1} (feasible if inventory or DIY available).
  - Attempt procure_masks (0/1), governed by supply/affordability; update m_i,t when fulfilled.
  - Send_messages to up to B_i neighbors (stochastic per active edge).
  - Comply_with_enforcement event if selected (pay fine; no immediate override of choice but updates perceptions).
- Interfaces with environment/platform
  - Receives exogenous signals: case rates, weather/seasonality, media sentiment, policy parameters (start Day 10), supply/subsidy.
  - Cannot change network topology or policy; can only influence neighbors via observed behavior/messages.
- Randomness & reproducibility
  - Individual parameters (β’s, traits, budgets) drawn from specified distributions stratified by age/income/degree; ε_i,t i.i.d. logistic or normal; message transmission and enforcement events are Bernoulli with scenario-set rates; all seeded for reproducibility.

Policy Authority
- Roles
  - Broadcaster of information campaigns; mandate setter; enforcement allocator; subsidy/mask-supply allocator.
- Observation
  - Observes aggregate indicators (citywide adoption rate, switching rates, case rates) and subgroup summaries; no individual-level perfect information unless scenario allows sampled audits.
- Communication
  - Broadcasts globally and/or targets subsets (e.g., high-degree nodes, workplaces, low-income quintiles) with controllable intensity; messages update residents’ perceived risk and norms weighted by recipient trust.
- Resources & constraints
  - Budget for campaigns, subsidies, and enforcement; maximum daily enforcement coverage; policy can change at specified times (baseline onset Day 10).
- Decision policy
  - By default follows exogenously specified schedules per scenario (timing/intensity of mandates, enforcement probability/coverage, fine level, campaign intensity/targeting, subsidy/supply levels); optional adaptive variants may adjust based on observed aggregate adoption.
- Action set (daily)
  - Set Mandate_t ∈ [0,1]; set Enforcement_t (coverage/probability) and Fine_t ($); set Campaign_t (intensity, targeting distribution); set Supply_t and Subsidy_t (price offsets, eligibility).
- Interfaces
  - Writes to environment-level signals consumed by residents; does not directly modify individual choices beyond altering incentives and information.
overview.interaction_topology:
interaction_topology: Primary pattern = multiplex (typed, weighted) social graph plus group broadcast; optional event bus for enforcement and procurement fulfillment.

- Nodes and layers
  - Nodes: Residents (all citizens). One Policy Authority node exists only as a broadcaster/controller, not as a peer in the graph.
  - Layers (edge types): household (home), workplace/school (work), community (comm).
  - Edges are undirected in membership but influence is effectively asymmetric through recipient-specific weights (trust/traits). No spatial layout.

- Graph construction (static topology; activation is dynamic)
  - Household: clique per household_id using empirical household-size distribution; strong clustering.
  - Workplace/school: affiliation clusters (coworkers/classmates connected) with degree heterogeneity; active mainly Mon–Fri.
  - Community: degree-targeted small-world/Chung–Lu with triadic closure to achieve realistic clustering and heavy-tailed degree; influencers are high-degree/high-centrality nodes on this layer.
  - No rewiring during the run; only activation varies by day.

- Edge weights and roles
  - Influence weights by layer: w_home ≈ 1.0 > w_work ≈ 0.7 > w_comm ≈ 0.5 (scenario-tunable).
  - Visibility by layer for implicit observation: v_home ≈ 0.95, v_work ≈ 0.80, v_comm ≈ 0.70; misclassification ε_home ≈ 0.02, ε_work ≈ 0.05, ε_comm ≈ 0.08; all subject to 1-day lag.
  - Messaging propensity by layer (sender side): σ_home > σ_work > σ_comm; constrained by sender budget B_i.

- Activation schedule (which edges “exist” for interaction on a given day)
  - Home: always active (α_home = 1.0).
  - Work/school: α_work = 0.9 weekdays, 0.1 weekends.
  - Community: α_comm = 0.8 weekdays, 1.2 weekends.
  - Only active edges count for observation, messaging, and enforcement exposure that day.

- Information flow on the graph
  - Implicit signaling: each resident’s mask_state_t is visible to neighbors on active edges with the specified v_l, ε_l, and 1-day lag.
  - Explicit interpersonal messages: per day, each resident can contact up to B_i neighbors across active edges; edges carry type-specific send probabilities and recipient trust weights; messages transmit normative cues and perceived risk.
  - Local aggregation: each resident computes layer-specific perceived prevalence p̂_i,l(t) via EWMA of observed neighbor masking on active edges; combines layers using w_l (and agent traits) to form the social-norm signal used in decisions.

- Group broadcast channel (secondary topology)
  - Citywide signals (Mandate_t ∈ [0,1], Enforcement coverage/probability, Fine_t, Campaign_t intensity/targeting, Supply_t, Subsidy_t, case rates, media sentiment) are broadcast globally each day.
  - Targeting: broadcasts can be restricted to subsets (e.g., high-degree quantiles, workplaces, income quintiles); receipt is probabilistic by recipient and filtered by government/media trust (τ_i, μ_i).
  - Broadcast does not alter graph edges; it updates agent-level perceived risk, norms, enforcement, and affordability signals.

- Enforcement exposure topology (event bus over public layers)
  - The Authority publishes an enforcement coverage/probability; the platform samples candidates among non-masked residents reachable via active public edges (work + community) that day; selected agents receive fine events.
  - Enforcement does not create edges; it leverages the day’s active-context reachability.

- Procurement/supply interaction (lightweight market abstraction)
  - No explicit retailer nodes by default. A citywide supply pool S_t and price P_t (post-subsidy) are broadcast.
  - Each procurement attempt is a Bernoulli match with success probability increasing in S_t and decreasing in aggregate demand; fulfilled orders generate delivery events after agent-specific lead time L_i.
  - Optional sensitivity variant: one-shot bipartite matching to a sampled set of retailers with capacities when needed.

- Constraints and scalability
  - Topology is static and aspatial; only activation and broadcasts vary over time.
  - Per-layer adjacency lists support O(deg) local updates; N ≈ 10^4–10^5.
  - Stochastic processes (activation, message delivery, enforcement sampling, procurement success) are seeded for reproducibility.

design_concepts.state_taxonomy:
state_taxonomy: Two agent types (Residents and Policy Authority) maintain static attributes, dynamic behavioral/psychological states, and finite memory with decay; observability is local, noisy, and lagged for Residents, aggregate for the Authority.

Residents (primary agents)
- Static (time-invariant or very slow-moving)
  - id; agent_type=resident; influencer_flag ∈ {0,1}.
  - Demographics: age_band, income_quintile ∈ {1..5}, education_level, health_vulnerability ∈ {0,1}.
  - Roles and network embedding: household_id and role (guardian/child), workplace_id/school_id or unemployed/retired flag, layer degrees (deg_home, deg_work, deg_comm), centrality_rank/quantile (for reporting/targeting).
  - Economic/stock constraints: initial mask inventory m_i,0 (units), desired buffer b_i ∈ [0,14], affordability threshold θ_aff ∈ [0,1] (max price share of daily/weekly budget), DIY_option ∈ {0,1}, subsidy_eligibility ∈ {0,1}, procurement lead time L_i ∈ {0..7} days.
  - Messaging: daily message budget B_i (default 5; influencers 20).
  - Preference/trait priors (drawn at init; may drift slowly): β0_i (utility intercept), conformity ω_i0, pro-sociality φ_i0, risk sensitivity κ_i0, government trust τ_i0, media trust μ_i0; discomfort baseline c_i,base; habit baseline h_i,0; price sensitivity β_Pi; media responsiveness β_Mi; social influence weight β_Si; risk responsiveness β_Ri; mandate/enforcement responsiveness β_Gi.
- Behavioral/Psychological (time-varying decision inputs)
  - mask_state_t ∈ {0,1} (action realized).
  - Intention/utility U_i(t) (latent) and compliance probability p_i(t)=sigmoid(U_i(t)).
  - Habit strength h_i(t) ∈ [0,1] (increases with consecutive masked days).
  - Fatigue/discomfort cost c_i,t ≥ 0 (rises with long masked streaks, decays with rest).
  - Perceived risk r̂_i(t) ∈ [0,1] (from case rates/media/policy).
  - Perceived enforcement Ê_i(t) ∈ [0,1] (from policy signals and recent fines).
  - Perceived net price P̂_i(t) (after subsidy/supply).
  - Layer-specific perceived prevalence p̂_i,l(t) ∈ [0,1] for l∈{home,work,comm}.
  - Procurement propensity q_i(t) ∈ [0,1] when m_i,t < b_i.
  - Messaging send propensity σ_i,l(t) per active edge type l.
- Memory (finite, decayed or bounded)
  - Neighbor masking memory per layer: EWMA with half-life HL_prevalence ≈ 7 days; computed only on edges active that day; retains last k=7 observations with exponential decay λ.
  - Case-risk memory r̂_i(t): EWMA of city case rate/media sentiment (half-life 5–10 days).
  - Enforcement memory: fine_received_within_τ ∈ {0,1} and last_fine_day; τ ≈ 14 days; counts of enforcement encounters seen by self (not others).
  - Habit/fatigue memory: consecutive_masked_days and consecutive_unmasked_days; last_switch_day.
  - Inventory/backorder: m_i,t (units on hand), outstanding_order ∈ {0,1}, expected_arrival_day.
  - Message memory: decayed sum of campaign/interpersonal exposures over last k_msg=7 days.
- Observable vs latent (Residents)
  - Self-observable (perfect, no lag): own past actions, m_i,t, outstanding_order, fines paid, received messages, b_i, B_i.
  - Socially observable to neighbors: current mask_state_t on active edges only; neighbors’ view is noisy (misclassification ε_l ∈ [0,0.1]) and one-day lagged; they cannot see messages unless explicitly sent.
  - Perception inputs from environment (broadcast, possibly filtered by τ_i, μ_i): mandate intensity ∈ [0,1], enforcement coverage/probability, fine level ($), campaign intensity/targeting exposure, supply S_t, subsidy level, city case rate, media sentiment, day-of-week, weather; no foresight of future policies.
  - Unobservable to others: U_i(t), traits {ω_i, φ_i, κ_i, τ_i, μ_i}, β’s, r̂_i(t), Ê_i(t), P̂_i(t), c_i,t, h_i(t), inventory m_i,t, procurement/backorder state, message decisions (unless received), perceived prevalences p̂_i,l(t).
  - Unobservable to self: true global adoption, distant-network states, true enforcement probability beyond signals and own experience.

Policy Authority (secondary agent)
- Static
  - id; agent_type=policy_authority; budgets for campaigns/subsidies/enforcement; max daily enforcement capacity; allowable targeting schemas; policy change windows; baseline strategy (exogenous schedule vs adaptive controller flag).
- Behavioral/Psychological (time-varying controls)
  - Mandate_t ∈ [0,1]; Enforcement_t: coverage/probability in [0,1]; Fine_t ≥ 0 ($); Campaign_t: intensity ≥ 0 and targeting distribution over groups/layers; Supply_t (mask units available) and Subsidy_t (price offset/eligibility rules).
- Memory
  - Time series buffers (last 30–40 days) of adoption rate A_t (overall and by subgroup), switching rates, cascade indicators, budgets spent/remaining, case rates; last_policy_change_day; optional controller state (e.g., error integrator for adaptive schemes).
- Observability and privacy (Authority)
  - Observes aggregates only: A_t overall, subgroup adoption/gaps (age/income/degree quantiles), switching rates, case rates, enforcement utilization, campaign reach; may observe sampled audits of compliance if scenario enables.
  - Does not observe individual latent traits or full network topology; cannot see per-edge perceptions or inventories.
  - Its chosen policy signals are globally observable to Residents (subject to exposure/trust filtering).

Platform-level logging (for evaluation, not exposed to agents)
- Ground-truth agent-level mask_state_t, fines, procurements, messages sent/received counts, inventories; aggregate time series; parameter draws; stochastic seeds. Agents do not access this log.
design_concepts.decision_policy_family:
Hybrid: rule-pruned random-utility (binary logit) with diffusion signal, plus rule-based heuristics for procurement/messaging; Authority is schedule-based with an optional adaptive variant. Uncertainty enters via random coefficients, logistic random utility, and stochastic exposure/sampling; all draws share seeded RNG streams.

Residents (mask-wearing decision, once per day)
- Feasibility pruning (rule-based): action set = {mask=1, mask=0} constrained by inventory (m_i,t>0) or DIY option. If p_i(t) recommends mask=1 but no inventory and no DIY, action is forced to 0; if DIY, apply higher discomfort cost via U_i(t).
- Random-utility binary logit (primary): compute latent utility U_i(t) = intercept + habit/inertia + social prevalence by layer (EWMA of observed neighbors × layer weights × conformity) + perceived epidemic risk × risk sensitivity + mandate×enforcement×trust − discomfort/fatigue − net price/affordability + media sentiment × media trust + idiosyncratic shock ε_i,t. ε_i,t ~ Logistic(0, s) with scale s=1 (temperature), scenario-tunable.
- Adoption probability: p_i(t) = sigmoid(U_i(t)). Action sampled as Bernoulli(p_i(t)).
- Heterogeneity: agent-specific coefficients (β’s, trait weights) drawn at initialization from stratified distributions (age/income/degree), fixed over time; these govern sensitivity to social influence, risk, mandate/enforcement, price, media, and inertia.
- Diffusion interpretation: the social-norm signal enters U_i(t) as a weighted average of perceived masking among active neighbors; thus the policy is both a threshold/diffusion rule (via sigmoid) and a random-utility discrete choice.
- Special household rule: minors mirror guardian household majority with probability ρ_home; otherwise they follow the same random-utility choice. This acts before Bernoulli sampling when applicable.

Residents (ancillary daily decisions)
- Procurement: rule-triggered with stochastic intensity. If inventory m_i,t < buffer b_i and no outstanding order, attempt purchase with probability q_i(t) = sigmoid(α0 + αS·Supply_t − αP·NetPrice_t/θ_aff + αR·perceived risk); success and delivery are handled by environment, not by the agent’s policy. Parameters α• heterogeneous by income and trust.
- Messaging: budget-limited probabilistic sending. Up to B_i contacts sampled among active edges; per-edge send probability σ_l by layer (home > work > community), scaled by agent type (influencers higher) and current motivation (e.g., higher when recent U_i(t) is strongly pro-mask). Recipients’ update is via their perception process; send/no-send is sampled Bernoulli(σ_i,l(t)) per candidate edge.

Policy Authority
- Primary: schedule-based controller. Mandate intensity, enforcement coverage/probability and fine level, campaign intensity/targeting, and supply/subsidy follow an exogenous time schedule (baseline onset Day 10). No direct optimization each day under the default setting.
- Optional adaptive variant: proportional control targeting an adoption trajectory A*; e.g., Mandate_t = clip(Mandate_{t-1} + kP·(A*_{t} − A_{t-1}), 0,1); enforcement/campaign scaled similarly subject to budgets. Randomness only in exposure/filtering at residents.

Uncertainty and sampling conventions
- Perception noise: neighbor masking observations are noisy and 1-day lagged with layer-specific misclassification; aggregated via EWMA.
- Random utility: ε_i,t ~ Logistic(0,1). Temperature can be tuned to match observed switching rates.
- Stochastic events: messaging sends, procurement attempts/success, enforcement selection, and campaign exposure are Bernoulli or multinomial draws with parameters set by scenario and agent traits.
- Reproducibility: common random numbers with stratified streams (utility noise, messaging, procurement, enforcement) under a global seed; tie-breaking is random only when scores are equal after pruning.
design_concepts.environment_and_signals:
environment_and_signals: Environment is aspatial, daily-updating (1-day tick; Day 0–Day 39), with a fixed multiplex social network as context. Exogenous signals are broadcast at the start of each day, are seed-controlled for reproducibility, and are bounded. Unless noted, Residents receive them same-day, filtered by their trust parameters (government τ_i, media μ_i) and stochastic exposure; the Policy Authority sees aggregate outcomes and can set policy signals (treated as exogenous to Residents).

- Timebase and observability
  - Update frequency: daily at tick t ∈ {0,…,39}.
  - Broadcast latency: 0 days (same-day), except interpersonal observations (handled elsewhere).
  - Residents observe signals with probability/exposure modifiers determined by τ_i, μ_i and campaign reach; perceived values can include small additive noise where stated.
  - Bounds: all indices clipped to [0,1]; prices ≥ $0; rates ≥ 0.

- Epidemic risk and derived perceptions
  - CityCaseRate_t (cases per 100k): exogenous epidemiological indicator; base + trend + weekly seasonality + noise; floor at 0.
    - Generation (default): start C_0 = 30/100k; multiplicative growth 1.08/day until Day 14; then decline 0.95/day thereafter. Weekly seasonality ±10% via sin(2πt/7). Additive noise ~ N(0, 5) clipped so C_t ≥ 0.
  - RiskIndex_t ∈ [0,1]: logistic transform of CityCaseRate_t, RiskIndex_t = 1/(1+exp(-γ·(CityCaseRate_t − C_mid))) with γ = 0.08, C_mid = 150/100k; optional 1-day smoothing (EWMA α=0.5). This is the environment’s clean risk signal.
    - Observability: Residents perceive r̂ signal as RiskIndex_t plus Gaussian noise N(0, 0.02) clipped to [0,1], then filtered by τ_i; this feeds r̂_i(t) via each agent’s EWMA memory.
  - WeatherHeatIndex_t ∈ [0,1]: exogenous thermal comfort proxy affecting mask discomfort.
    - Generation: weak sinusoid over horizon: 0.5 + 0.2·sin(2π(t−5)/20) + noise N(0,0.03); clip [0,1].
    - Impact: increases per-day discomfort c_i,t via additive term δ_C·(WeatherHeatIndex_t − 0.5), δ_C > 0 (scenario-set).

- Media and information environment
  - MediaSentiment_t ∈ [−1,1]: aggregate tone of media regarding masking and risk.
    - Generation: 0.6·(2·RiskIndex_t − 1) + 0.2·Mandate_t − Fatigue_t + noise N(0,0.15); clip [−1,1].
    - Fatigue_t ∈ [0,1]: policy/message wear-out, rises slowly after sustained mandates/campaigns: Fatigue_t = max(0, 0.02·max(0, t−15)) capped at 0.5 unless reset by shock.
    - Observability: Residents receive with media trust μ_i; enters U_i(t) via β_M μ_i·MediaSentiment_t.
  - ExogenousShockDays: optional list of days with abrupt changes (e.g., scandal, misinformation, supply disruption). On shock days, add step perturbation ΔMedia ∈ [−0.5,0.5] to MediaSentiment_t and/or ΔRisk ∈ [−0.2,0.2] to RiskIndex_t before clipping.

- Economic/supply signals for masks
  - SupplyIndex_t ∈ [0,1]: citywide relative availability (0=scarce, 1=abundant).
    - Schedule (baseline): 0.45 on Days 0–9; linear ramp to 0.8 by Day 15; 0.9 afterward. Optional shortage window Days 18–20: −0.25 (clip at 0.2).
  - PriceUSD_t ≥ 0: retail price per disposable unit (or per wear-equivalent).
    - Generation: baseline $1.50; inversely related to SupplyIndex_t: PriceUSD_t = max(0.5, 2.5 − 1.5·SupplyIndex_t) + noise N(0,0.05); clip [0.5,3.0].
  - SubsidyRate_t ∈ [0,1]: fraction price offset (global scalar; targeting handled via eligibility flags at agents).
    - Schedule (baseline): 0 until Day 11; 0.3 from Day 12 onward; optional increase to 0.5 on Day 20 under stronger intervention scenario.
  - NetPriceUSD_t: environment broadcasts PriceUSD_t and SubsidyRate_t; agents compute net price conditional on eligibility: NetPrice_i,t = PriceUSD_t·(1 − SubsidyRate_t·1[eligible_i]).
  - DeliveryLatencyBase_t (days) ∈ [0,7]: mean fulfillment lag; 3 days pre-intervention; improves with supply: DeliveryLatencyBase_t = round(5 − 3·SupplyIndex_t) with floor 0; stochastic per agent via their L_i.
  - ProcurementSuccessBase_t ∈ [0,1]: baseline per-attempt success probability curve used by the platform: clip(0.2 + 0.7·SupplyIndex_t, 0, 0.95); demand feedback reduces this internally via aggregate requests, but the broadcast baseline is exogenous guidance.

- Institutional/policy signals (Authority-controlled; exogenous to Residents)
  - Mandate_t ∈ [0,1]: strength of masking mandate (normative/legal).
    - Baseline schedule: 0 on Days 0–9; 0.6 on Days 10–19; 0.8 on Days 20–39.
    - Impact: enters U_i(t) via β_G τ_i·Mandate_t·EEnforce_t·FineScaled_t.
  - EnforceCoverage_t ∈ [0,1]: share of non-masked in public layers sampled for potential enforcement each day.
    - Baseline: 0 through Day 11; 0.05 Days 12–19; 0.10 Days 20–39.
  - EnforceProb_t ∈ [0,1]: probability a sampled violator is fined; baseline 0.5 constant.
  - FineUSD_t ≥ 0: monetary penalty; baseline $50 Days 10–19, $75 Days 20–39; cap $200.
  - EEnforce_t ∈ [0,1]: environment-broadcast perceived enforcement intensity summary for cognition: clip(EnforceCoverage_t·EnforceProb_t, 0,1). Residents combine with τ_i and personal fine memory.
  - CampaignIntensity_t ≥ 0: expected exposures per capita per day via public information campaigns; baseline 0 pre-Day 10; 0.4 Days 10–14; 0.8 Days 15–39. Effective impact decays with Fatigue_t (multiplicative factor 1 − 0.5·Fatigue_t).
  - CampaignTargetMix_t: shares over targeting groups (e.g., general 70%, high-degree 20%, low-income 10% after Day 10). Broadcast for transparency; receipt is probabilistic per agent.

- Calendar and activation modifiers
  - DayOfWeek_t ∈ {Mon,…,Sun} and WeekendFlag_t ∈ {0,1}; deterministic.
    - Impact: governs layer activation (work/school vs community) and enforcement focus on public layers; also modulates CampaignIntensity_t by +20% on weekdays for workplace-targeted outreach, +20% on weekends for community-targeted outreach.
  - HolidayFlag_t ∈ {0,1}: optional single-day events (e.g., Day 25) with higher community activation; if set, increase observed public interactions and enforcement sampling pool size by +30% that day (handled by platform), not a direct utility term.

- Noise, bounds, and seeds
  - All stochastic components draw from seeded streams; per-signal noise is independent across days unless otherwise noted.
  - Clipping rules: indices ∈ [0,1]; MediaSentiment_t ∈ [−1,1]; prices ≥ $0.5; FineUSD_t ≤ $200.

- Impact pathways summary (into agents/platform)
  - RiskIndex_t → r̂_i(t) (after trust/noise/memory) → U_i(t) via β_R κ_i.
  - MediaSentiment_t (filtered by μ_i) → U_i(t) via β_M.
  - WeatherHeatIndex_t → discomfort c_i,t (raising masking disutility).
  - Mandate_t, EEnforce_t, FineUSD_t → U_i(t) via β_G τ_i; fines update enforcement memory and affordability.
  - SupplyIndex_t, PriceUSD_t, SubsidyRate_t → procurement attempt probability q_i(t), success rates, delivery latency; NetPrice_i,t also enters U_i(t) via price term and affordability constraint.
  - CampaignIntensity_t and CampaignTargetMix_t → exposure counts for message reception; exposures update message memory and perceived norms/risk.
  - DayOfWeek/Holiday → platform edge activation and enforcement sampling context, indirectly affecting perceived prevalence and observed fines.

- Scenario switches and levers (all daily, piecewise-constant unless specified)
  - Start of intervention: Day 10 (Mandate_t>0, CampaignIntensity_t>0; enforcement can lag to Day 12).
  - Intensity ramps: Mandate_t and EnforceCoverage_t step up again on Day 20 in baseline; alternative scenarios can shift timing ±5 days or adjust magnitudes within [0,1].
  - Supply and subsidy: ramp SupplyIndex_t earlier/later; adjust SubsidyRate_t ∈ [0,1]; introduce/remedy shortages.
  - Shock toggles: enable media shocks, supply disruptions, or sudden case surges for counterfactuals.
  - All levers are bounded and seed-controlled to ensure reproducible scenario generation and agent-facing signals.
design_concepts.actions_and_constraints:
Actions
- Residents (once per day unless noted)
  - SetMaskState: choose mask_state_t ∈ {1=wear, 0=not wear}.
  - AttemptProcureMasks: submit at most one purchase request if inventory below buffer; creates or updates an outstanding order.
  - SendMessages: select up to B_i neighbors on active edges and attempt to send normative/risk messages (probabilistic per edge).
  - DIYMaskUse: implicit variant of SetMaskState when inventory is zero but DIY_option=1 (incurs higher discomfort cost).
  - ComplyAndSettleFine: if selected by enforcement, pay fine; no choice to refuse (platform-enforced).
  - NoOp: take no additional action beyond mask decision (default if other actions are infeasible or budgets exhausted).

- Policy Authority (once per day)
  - SetMandate(level): choose Mandate_t ∈ [0,1].
  - SetEnforcement(coverage, probability, fine): choose EnforceCoverage_t ∈ [0,1], EnforceProb_t ∈ [0,1], FineUSD_t ≥ 0.
  - AllocateCampaign(intensity, targeting): choose CampaignIntensity_t ≥ 0 and targeting mix over groups.
  - SetSupplyAndSubsidy: choose SupplyIndex_t ∈ [0,1] (availability proxy) and SubsidyRate_t ∈ [0,1].
  - NoOp: carry over prior settings (default outside change windows).

Constraints
- Global timing and frequency
  - Daily tick; each resident may execute at most one SetMaskState, ≤1 AttemptProcureMasks, and ≤B_i SendMessages per day. Authority may update each control at most once per day.
  - Edge activation windows constrain SendMessages (only on active edges that day) and enforcement candidate pools (public layers only).
  - Broadcasts (Authority controls and exogenous signals) occur before resident actions; enforcement sampling occurs after resident mask choices; deliveries occur at end-of-day when due.

- Feasibility by action
  - SetMaskState
    - Feasible wear (1) if m_i,t > 0 or DIY_option=1; otherwise forced to 0 (fallback).
    - Exactly one choice per day; minors may mirror household guardian majority with probability ρ_home but must still satisfy feasibility.
  - AttemptProcureMasks
    - Allowed only if m_i,t < b_i and no outstanding_order; ≤1 attempt/day.
    - Attempt requires affordability: NetPrice_i,t ≤ θ_aff·(agent budget proxy); otherwise infeasible.
  - SendMessages
    - Limited to active edges; cannot target the same neighbor more than once per day; total sends ≤ B_i; per-edge send governed by σ_l and agent motivation.
  - DIYMaskUse
    - Only when m_i,t=0 and DIY_option=1; increases daily discomfort cost c_i,t (handled in decision utility).
  - ComplyAndSettleFine
    - Triggered only if agent is sampled while mask_state_t=0 on public layers; mandatory payment when triggered.

- Capacity and competition
  - Procurement
    - Citywide fulfillment limited by SupplyIndex_t; if aggregate demand exceeds capacity, requests are resolved by lottery without replacement; unsuccessful attempts may create backorders with delivery latency L_i drawn around DeliveryLatencyBase_t.
  - Enforcement
    - Maximum daily enforcements constrained by EnforceCoverage_t and operational capacity; non-masked candidates on active public edges are sampled without replacement; each sampled agent is fined with probability EnforceProb_t.
  - Campaign exposure
    - CampaignIntensity_t and targeting define expected exposures; realized exposures are bounded by budget and delivered via probabilistic assignment.

- Budgets and affordability
  - Residents face affordability thresholds θ_aff; NetPrice_i,t incorporates SubsidyRate_t and eligibility; fines (FineUSD_t) reduce future effective affordability (tighten θ_aff or reduce procurement propensity).
  - Authority controls are bounded by budgets: daily campaign intensity, subsidies, supply boosts, and enforcement coverage cannot exceed available budget/capacity; infeasible settings are clipped or rejected.

- Norms and regulatory constraints
  - Mandate_t does not prohibit mask_state_t=0 but enables enforcement and affects perceived utility.
  - Fines apply only to mask_state_t=0 observed in public contexts; no fines at home.

- Conservation and accounting
  - Inventory m_i,t decreases by 1 if mask_state_t=1 (clip at ≥0); deliveries add units on due day; at most one outstanding_order per agent; no negative inventory.
  - Message budget B_i resets daily; unused capacity does not carry over.
  - Monetary quantities (prices, fines) are nonnegative; cumulative_fines and spend are tracked for affordability effects.

- Eligibility and permissions
  - Subsidy eligibility flag gates access to SubsidyRate_t.
  - Influencer_flag expands messaging capacity (higher B_i) and may modify σ_l; otherwise same feasibility rules.
  - Enforcement applies only to residents; Authority is exempt.

- Exclusivity and collision
  - An agent cannot both wear and not wear a mask on the same day; cannot place multiple orders concurrently; cannot send multiple messages to the same neighbor in the same day.
  - Authority cannot set conflicting controls beyond bounds; last-in-day setting prevails.

- Precedence and ordering
  - Signal receipt → resident decisions (SetMaskState, AttemptProcureMasks, SendMessages) → enforcement sampling/fines → deliveries → inventory consumption for mask_state_t=1 → state logging.
  - Procurement attempts precede delivery; outstanding orders block new attempts until resolved.

- Safety, bounds, and clipping
  - All probabilities ∈ [0,1]; prices ≥ $0.5; FineUSD_t ≤ $200; SupplyIndex_t ∈ [0,1]; variables are clipped to bounds if controls propose out-of-range values.

- Fallbacks
  - Infeasible SetMaskState=1 due to inventory shortfall and DIY_option=0 falls back to SetMaskState=0.
  - Infeasible procurement (affordability, outstanding order, or capacity) falls back to no order (or backorder if enabled).
  - Messaging over-budget or without active edges falls back to no message.
  - If multiple agents compete for scarce procurement or enforcement slots, lottery resolves conflicts; unserved agents wait until next day.

details.scenarios_and_interventions:
scenarios_and_interventions: We define comparable “worlds” that differ only in exogenous signals and policy schedules, while holding network, population, and random seeds constant (unless noted). Each intervention specifies trigger, intensity, duration, and fatigue/adaptation. All time is in days (0–39). Unless changed below, unspecified signals/parameters follow the environment defaults.

- S0 No-Policy Counterfactual (control)
  - Trigger: None (Mandate, Enforcement, Campaign, Subsidy all off for all t).
  - Intensity: Mandate_t=0; EnforceCoverage_t=0; EnforceProb_t=0; FineUSD_t=0; CampaignIntensity_t=0; SubsidyRate_t=0. SupplyIndex_t and PriceUSD_t follow default exogenous schedule; RiskIndex_t, MediaSentiment_t as generated (no policy coupling).
  - Duration: Entire horizon.
  - Fatigue/Adaptation: Only endogenous (habit/fatigue, memory decay); no policy fatigue.

- S1 Reference Baseline (default schedule with Day-10 onset; matches blueprint)
  - Trigger: Fixed dates.
    - Mandate: t≥10; step-up at t=20.
    - Enforcement: coverage on t≥12; step-up at t=20; EnforceProb constant.
    - Campaign: t≥10; ramp at t=15.
    - Subsidy: t≥12.
  - Intensity:
    - Mandate_t=0 (t<10), 0.6 (10–19), 0.8 (20–39).
    - EnforceCoverage_t=0 (t<12), 0.05 (12–19), 0.10 (20–39); EnforceProb_t=0.5; FineUSD_t=$50 (10–19), $75 (20–39).
    - CampaignIntensity_t=0.4 (10–14), 0.8 (15–39) with baseline targeting mix: general 70%, high-degree 20%, low-income 10%.
    - SubsidyRate_t=0 (t<12), 0.3 (t≥12).
    - SupplyIndex_t: 0.45 (0–9), linear ramp to 0.8 by t=15, then 0.9; no shortage window in this scenario. PriceUSD_t as implied by supply.
  - Duration: From first trigger until t=39.
  - Fatigue/Adaptation: Campaign effectiveness reduced by Fatigue_t (media wear-out); perceived enforcement decays via personal fine memory τ≈14 days; residents’ habit/fatigue and risk memory per defaults. No explicit mandate-salience decay beyond these mechanisms.

- S2 Early & Strong Intervention (front-loaded, higher intensity)
  - Trigger: Fixed early start.
    - Mandate: t≥5; step-ups at t=12 and t=20.
    - Enforcement: t≥7; step-up at t=12 and t=20.
    - Campaign: t≥5; ramp at t=10.
    - Subsidy: t≥7.
  - Intensity:
    - Mandate_t=0.5 (5–11), 0.7 (12–19), 0.9 (20–39).
    - EnforceCoverage_t=0.06 (7–11), 0.10 (12–19), 0.15 (20–39); EnforceProb_t=0.6; FineUSD_t=$60 (5–19), $90 (20–39).
    - CampaignIntensity_t=0.6 (5–9), 1.0 (10–39); targeting: general 50%, high-degree 40%, low-income 10%.
    - SubsidyRate_t=0.4 (t≥7).
    - SupplyIndex_t boosted by +0.1 from default (clip ≤1) to ensure procurement feasibility.
  - Duration: Policies stay active once triggered.
  - Fatigue/Adaptation: Stronger campaign incurs faster fatigue: multiply CampaignIntensity_t by (1 − min(0.6, 0.03·max(0, t−10))). Enforcement memory and resident habit/fatigue as default.

- S3 Late & Weak Intervention (delayed and milder)
  - Trigger: Fixed late start.
    - Mandate: t≥15; step-up at t=25.
    - Enforcement: t≥17; step-up at t=25.
    - Campaign: t≥15.
    - Subsidy: t≥17.
  - Intensity:
    - Mandate_t=0.4 (15–24), 0.6 (25–39).
    - EnforceCoverage_t=0.03 (17–24), 0.06 (25–39); EnforceProb_t=0.5; FineUSD_t=$40 (15–24), $60 (25–39).
    - CampaignIntensity_t=0.3 (15–39); targeting: general 80%, high-degree 10%, low-income 10%.
    - SubsidyRate_t=0.2 (t≥17).
    - Supply/Price default.
  - Duration: From triggers to t=39.
  - Fatigue/Adaptation: Standard fatigue only (as baseline); weaker salience yields lower perceived enforcement even with same EnforceProb via EEnforce_t product.

- S4 High-Signal Risk Environment (exogenous amplification without changing policy schedule)
  - Trigger: Always on (t=0–39).
  - Intensity:
    - RiskIndex_t amplified: RiskIndex’_t = clip(0.5 + 1.2·(RiskIndex_t − 0.5), 0, 1); volatility +50%: add N(0, 0.03) before clipping.
    - MediaSentiment_t follows default coupling to risk/mandate; no policy changes (use S1 schedule).
  - Duration: Entire horizon.
  - Fatigue/Adaptation: As in S1; higher perceived risk elevates sustained masking but also increases discomfort via longer wear streaks (endogenous fatigue).

- S5 Media Shock & Polarization (information shock counteracting mandates)
  - Trigger: Negative media shock at t=22; partial trust dampening t=22–28.
  - Intensity:
    - MediaSentiment_t step Δ=−0.4 at t=22 (clip [−1,1]) then linearly recovers to baseline by t=29.
    - Government/media trust attenuation for a random 40% of residents (stratified by income quintile so low-income more exposed): τ_i → 0.8·τ_i, μ_i → 0.7·μ_i for t∈[22,28]; reverts thereafter.
    - Policies follow S1 schedule.
  - Duration: Shock window t=22–28 for trust; sentiment recovers by t=29.
  - Fatigue/Adaptation: Campaign effectiveness additionally reduced by +0.1 to Fatigue_t during shock window (clip ≤0.6). Agents’ memories smooth recovery via EWMA.

- S6 Supply Shortage + Subsidy Boost (economic countermeasure)
  - Trigger: Supply disruption t=18–20; immediate subsidy response t=18 onward.
  - Intensity:
    - SupplyIndex_t −=0.5 (clip ≥0.2) for t=18–20; DeliveryLatencyBase_t increases accordingly; ProcurementSuccessBase_t drops per supply.
    - SubsidyRate_t increases to 0.5 at t=18 (from S1’s 0.3) and persists.
    - Policies otherwise follow S1.
  - Duration: Shortage t=18–20; subsidy persists to t=39.
  - Fatigue/Adaptation: Temporary inventory constraints raise DIY use and discomfort; after shortage, procurement rebounds; no additional policy fatigue beyond S1.

- S7 Adaptive Controller (feedback policy aiming for target adoption)
  - Trigger: Active from t=10.
  - Intensity (updated daily using proportional control; clipped to bounds):
    - Target trajectory A*_{t} = min(0.9, 0.4 + 0.02·(t−10)) for t≥10.
    - Mandate_t = clip(Mandate_{t−1} + k_M·(A*_{t} − A_{t−1}), 0, 1) with k_M=0.8.
    - EnforceCoverage_t = clip(EnforceCoverage_{t−1} + k_E·(A*_{t} − A_{t−1}), 0, 0.2) with k_E=0.2; EnforceProb_t=0.5; FineUSD_t=$50 (t<20), $75 (t≥20).
    - CampaignIntensity_t = clip(CampaignIntensity_{t−1} + k_C·(A*_{t} − A_{t−1}), 0, 1.2) with k_C=1.5; targeting shifts 40% to top-degree quintile when A_{t−1}<0.6 else revert to baseline mix.
    - SubsidyRate_t=0.3 (t≥12) unless A_{t−1}<0.5 and PriceUSD_t>1.2, then 0.5 for that day.
    - Initialize at t=9 with Mandate_9=0, EnforceCoverage_9=0, CampaignIntensity_9=0.
  - Duration: t=10–39 (controller remains on).
  - Fatigue/Adaptation: Campaign fatigue per Fatigue_t; controller reacts to diminished returns by raising intensity within bounds; no explicit decay of mandate effect beyond existing mechanisms.

- S8 Targeted High-Degree Outreach (network-aware intervention)
  - Trigger: t≥10 (coincides with mandate onset).
  - Intensity:
    - CampaignIntensity_t=0.8 (10–39); 60% of exposures targeted to top 20% by community-layer degree, 20% to workplaces, 20% general.
    - Mandate/Enforcement/Subsidy follow S1.
  - Duration: t=10–39.
  - Fatigue/Adaptation: Same fatigue as S1; higher local norm acceleration around hubs; diminishing marginal campaign returns appear via Fatigue_t.

Implementation notes
- All scenarios use the same network and agent parameter draws; scenario differences are exclusively in signals/policies above. Common RNG seeds per stream ensure comparability; when a scenario adds randomness (e.g., S5 trust attenuation sampling), a fixed sub-seed is used.
- Outputs are logged identically per scenario for cross-arm evaluation, with forecast focus on Days 30–39.
details.evidence_calibration_evaluation:
Evidence / Data Anchoring
- Input data (drivers/constraints; daily cadence, Day 0–39 unless noted)
  - Agent attributes: synthetic population matched to city marginals (age bands, income quintiles, household sizes, employment/school status, degree distributions per layer). Sources: census-style tabulations and labor/school rosters or public summaries. Preprocessing: raking to joint distributions; assign roles and eligibility flags; draw psychosocial trait priors from stratified priors; document RNG seed and sampling recipe.
  - Networks (multiplex): household cliques from household roster; workplace/school affiliation graphs built from establishment/class sizes; community layer from degree-targeted Chung–Lu with triadic closure calibrated to observed clustering and degree tail. Store adjacency by layer and activation modifiers by day-of-week.
  - Historical behaviors: observed (or proxy) daily mask-wearing states for Days 0–29 at agent-level when available, else subgroup-level adoption rates and switching rates (overall and by age/income/degree quantiles). If only aggregates exist, use them as calibration targets; if microdata exist, use them for micro-fit.
  - Policy timelines: mandate levels, enforcement coverage/probability, fines, campaign intensity/targeting, subsidies/supply from administrative logs; confirm Day 10 onset and subsequent steps (or scenario-specific schedules).
  - Exogenous indicators: city case rates; media sentiment index; weather/heat index; price and supply signals; day-of-week and holidays. Preprocessing: clip to stated bounds; smooth with EWMA as specified; align time zones; impute missing days via linear interpolation (≤2-day gaps) or last-observation-carried-forward with uncertainty inflation.
- Target indicators / observables (to fit/validate)
  - Daily adoption rate A_t (overall and by subgroups), switching rates, fines issued, procurement attempts/success, and cascade summaries (e.g., fraction of nodes adopting within k days of a neighbor’s adoption).
  - Agent-level mask states for Days 0–29 (when available) for classification training; Days 30–39 strictly held out for forecasting evaluation.
- Data splits
  - Temporal split: calibrate on Days 0–24; validate early on Days 25–29; test on Days 30–39. No parameter tuning against test-period outcomes.
  - If only aggregates exist: use rolling-origin backtesting within 0–29 for early stopping; freeze parameters then forecast 30–39.
  - Scenario-level splits: tune on Reference Baseline (S1) unless explicitly studying counterfactuals; evaluate generalization to S0–S8 without retuning (report both zero-shot and light-retune variants if allowed).

Calibration / Fitting and Segmentation
- Parameters to tune (bounded ranges; priors centered on blueprint values)
  - Social influence: β_S ∈ [0, 3]; layer weights multipliers w_home ∈ [0.7, 1.3], w_work ∈ [0.4, 1.0], w_comm ∈ [0.2, 0.8].
  - Risk responsiveness: β_R ∈ [−0.5, 3]; risk memory half-life HL_risk ∈ [5, 14] days.
  - Mandate/enforcement responsiveness: β_G ∈ [0, 3]; enforcement memory window τ ∈ [7, 21] days; perceived enforcement scaling multiplier ∈ [0.7, 1.3].
  - Habit/inertia and fatigue: β_H ∈ [0, 2]; habit gain per masked day ∈ [0.01, 0.15]; fatigue increment per consecutive masked day ∈ [0, 0.08], decay half-life ∈ [3, 10] days.
  - Price/cost: β_P ∈ [−3, 0]; discomfort baseline c_base multipliers by weather sensitivity δ_C ∈ [0, 0.6].
  - Media responsiveness: β_M ∈ [−0.5, 2]; media trust attenuation multiplier ∈ [0.7, 1.1] if evidence suggests.
  - Perception/memory of neighbor prevalence: HL_prevalence ∈ [3, 14] days; observation noise scalers per layer ±0.02 around defaults if empirical audits exist.
  - Temperature of logit (utility noise scale s) ∈ [0.6, 1.5].
  - Procurement propensity parameters: α0 ∈ [−2, 2], αS ∈ [0, 3], αP ∈ [0, 3], αR ∈ [0, 3]; desired buffer distribution mean ∈ [3, 10] units.
- Identification aids
  - Use Day-10 mandate onset and Day-12/20 enforcement step-ups as quasi-exogenous shifts to identify β_G and enforcement scaling via difference-in-differences between public-facing (work/community-active) vs home contexts and by trust strata.
  - Exploit supply/price variation and subsidy onset (Day 12) to identify β_P and procurement parameters.
  - Use heat index variation to inform discomfort coupling δ_C.
  - Day-of-week activation patterns help separate work vs community layer weights.
- Segmentation (group-specific multipliers or hierarchical priors)
  - Age bands: minors, 18–35, 36–64, 65+ (apply multipliers to β_S, β_R, β_G, β_P; e.g., higher β_R for 65+).
  - Income quintiles: adjust affordability θ_aff and β_P; subsidy eligibility effects.
  - Degree quantiles (by community layer): top 20% “hubs” vs others (higher β_S and messaging propensity; separate prior for influencers).
  - Trust clusters: high vs low government/media trust (τ_i, μ_i) via mixture priors.
  - Employment/school status: tune w_work and σ_work for employed/students versus retired/unemployed.
- Methods
  - Two-stage fit: (1) Hierarchical Bayesian logistic regression on Days 0–24 microdata (if available) to estimate β• with partial pooling across segments; (2) Simulation-based calibration (ABC-SMC or Bayesian optimization with Gaussian process surrogate) to refine social-layer weights, memory, habit/fatigue, and noise scale to minimize mismatch in aggregate targets on Days 0–24, with early stopping on Days 25–29.
  - Objective function (multi-term, weighted): J = w1·RMSE(A_t overall) + w2·Σ_groups RMSE(A_t^g) + w3·RMSE(switching_t) + w4·DTW(A_t) + w5·penalties for implausible rates (e.g., negative switching) + λ·regularization (L2 on deviations from priors). Weights set to balance scale; perform sensitivity analysis.
  - Optimization details: 200–500 simulations per iteration using common random numbers; trust-region Bayesian optimization or CMA-ES for continuous parameters; ABC tolerance shrinks over SMC generations. Enforce parameter bounds and monotonicity where applicable (e.g., β_P ≤ 0).
  - Validation: monitor overfitting via gap between 0–24 fit and 25–29 validation; stop when improvement on validation plateaus (Patience=3 iterations). Perform k-fold by households or workplaces if microdata; else rolling-origin within 0–29.
  - Robustness: perturb exogenous signals within reported noise bands; re-fit light-touch and report parameter stability (coefficients’ relative change <20% recommended).

Evaluation (forecast focus Days 30–39)
- Agent-level prediction (if microdata available for test window)
  - AUC and PR-AUC for mask=1; log loss; Brier score; Expected Calibration Error (ECE) with 10–20 bins; reliability diagrams; confusion-derived F1 for thresholded predictions calibrated to validation set.
- Aggregate time-series fit
  - RMSE/MAE on A_t overall and by subgroup; DTW distance and cosine similarity; peak timing error (days) and peak magnitude error (% points); time-to-thresholds (50%/70%/90%) absolute error; area-under-adoption-curve difference over 30–39.
- Distributional and event metrics
  - JS divergence or Wasserstein distance between simulated and observed switching-rate distributions; fines per day vs observed; procurement success rates vs observed; cascade size distribution overlap (e.g., KS statistic on k-neighborhood adoption bursts).
- Uncertainty quantification
  - 80% and 95% predictive interval coverage and mean/median width for A_t and subgroup A_t^g; PIT histograms for calibration of intervals. Construct via posterior draws and/or CRN-based ensembles.
- Fairness and subgroup parity
  - Gaps in MAE and calibration (ECE) across age/income/degree quantiles; disparity in time-to-70% adoption; Theil or Gini of adoption shares on Days 30–39; report effect sizes and confidence intervals.
- Scenario comparisons (S0–S8)
  - Δ adoption at t=39 vs S1; Δ time-to-threshold; Δ switching volatility; policy contribution decomposition (Mandate/Enforcement/Price/Media) via ablation runs; report standardized effect sizes.

Reproducibility
- Randomness control
  - Global base seed plus stratified RNG streams: (1) utility noise, (2) interpersonal messaging, (3) procurement attempts/success, (4) enforcement sampling/fines, (5) campaign exposures, (6) exogenous-signal noise, (7) network generation (if ever re-sampled). Common random numbers across calibration candidates and scenario comparisons.
- Configuration freezing
  - Immutable run configs (YAML/JSON) capturing: parameter priors/bounds, chosen optimum, scenario schedule, horizon, seeds, network snapshot ID, segmentation schema, objective weights, and software versions/compute environment. Store commit hash of code.
- Data versioning
  - Snapshot raw and processed datasets with checksums; retain preprocessing scripts and logs; record imputation decisions and uncertainty inflation factors.
- Logging and audit trail
  - Persist per-iteration calibration objective values, accepted parameter sets (ABC posterior or BO incumbent), validation metrics, and early-stopping triggers. Index all artifacts by run_id = {scenario}_{seed}_{date}_{code_hash}.
- Replication package
  - Provide scripts/notebooks to (a) rebuild synthetic population/network, (b) re-run calibration, (c) generate forecasts and metrics, (d) reproduce figures/tables. Include parameter cards and README with units/bounds.

Output Artifacts
- Tables (CSV or Parquet)
  - daily_timeseries_{scenario}_{seed}.csv: A_t overall; subgroup A_t^g; switching rates; fines; procurement stats; predictive intervals.
  - agent_states_day30_39_{scenario}_{seed}.parquet: agent-level mask_state, probabilities, inventories (subset for test window to limit size).
  - evaluation_summary_{scenario}.csv: metrics listed above for Days 30–39; subgroup fairness metrics; scenario deltas.
  - calibration_trace_{scenario}.csv: parameter candidates, objective components, acceptance flags, posterior weights (if ABC).
  - parameter_card_{scenario}.csv: final tuned parameters with bounds, segment multipliers, and uncertainty (CI/posterior SD).
- Figures
  - Time-series fits with fan charts (overall and key subgroups) for 0–39, highlighting 30–39.
  - Reliability diagrams; ROC/PR curves; PIT histograms.
  - DTW alignment plots; peak/time-to-threshold comparison bars.
  - Cascade and switching distribution overlays; fairness gap bar charts.
  - Scenario comparison panels (S0–S8) with Δ metrics and effect sizes.
- Documentation
  - Clear legends with units (adoption as fraction [0,1]; prices/fines in USD; exposures per capita per day); day indexing (0–39); scenario definitions; RNG seed disclosure; file naming scheme; axis labels and confidence band definitions.

original_research_topic:
description: Develop a multi-agent simulation system that models the spread of mask-wearing behavior through social networks.
simulation_focus: Predict agents' mask-wearing behavior over day 30 - day 39 (last ten days) based on their attributes, social connections, and past behavior
Model information propagation and behavioral changes triggered by social influence and government intervention starting on Day 10

data_files.agent_attributes.csv: Contains demographic and behavioral attributes of each agent, including age, occupation, risk perception, and social connection counts
data_files.social_network.json: Contains structured data representing a social network. Each entry corresponds to a user (identified by a unique integer ID), and the values describe the different types of relationships that user has with others. Data Structure: The top-level structure is a dictionary ({} in JSON). Keys: Each key is a unique user ID (as an integer, e.g., 0, 1, 2, etc.). Values: Each value is another dictionary with the following fields: "family": a list of user IDs representing family connections. "work_school": a list of user IDs representing colleagues or schoolmates. "community": a list of user IDs representing community-level acquaintances. "all": a merged list of all user IDs connected to the user across the three categories above.
data_files.train_data.csv: Time series data for the first 30 days, used for training the model

RMSE.description: Root Mean Square Error measuring overall predictive accuracy of mask adoption rates
RMSE.interpretation: Directly interpretable as percentage deviations due to the 0-1 range

Peak Adoption Rate Error.description: Measures model accuracy in predicting maximum mask adoption during intervention

Time-to-Peak Error.description: Measures model accuracy in predicting the time lag from intervention to peak behavior change
